newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania weather affects some grain areas -ministry.
newsitem.headline: Romania weather affects some grain areas -ministry.

text.p: Heavy rain and snowfalls in Romania over the past weeks have so far affected over 18,000 hectares of farmland sown to wheat and barley, the agriculture ministry said on Thursday.
Data issued by the ministry showed bad weather had affected 14,600 ha from a total of 2.4 million put under wheat as well as some 4,000 ha from a total 419,400 sown to barley.
"These are preliminary figures based on reports we received from across the country," a ministry official said.
"We'll have a complete picture by the end of the month," said the official.

Rain, snow and freezing temperatures swept the country over the past weeks. Rivers in eastern and central Romania also flooded large areas of cropland but farmers had managed to drain the water, reports in the local media said.
The ministry official said wheat growth "looks fine for this time of the year". But he said it was too early to give an estimate for the 1997 wheat crop.
Unofficial estimates in the Romanian media put Romania's 1997 wheat crop at around 6.0 million tonnes.

Last year, an early and prolonged winter damaged the crop on half of the area sown. That produced a harvest less than 60 percent of the 1995 bumper crop of some 7.8 million tonnes. Exports then amounted to 1.3 million tonnes.

On Wednesday, ministry data indicated density on 1,527,563 ha under wheat amounted to 400 stalks per square metre. A total of 757,547 ha had a density of 250 to 400 stalks per square metre, while 90,800 ha had less than 250 stalks per square metre.
Wheat germinated partially on 8,817 ha while 4,377 ha yielded no stalks so far, data showed.

Last month, the ministry said Romania might take some 550,000 tonnes of wheat from the strategic reserves and even resort to imports to meet demand for bread and bakery products until July, when the 1997 wheat crop is harvested.
